newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil holds off weaker crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil holds off weaker crude.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady at midday on Firday in quiet trade despite further falls to crude prices as the market looked to prompt demand a low stocks for support.
"The market is very quiet but it is steady," one broker said.
April gas oil was last quoted unchanged from Thursday at $26.70/$26.90 per barrel, brokers said. May was last quoted at $25.30/$25.40 per barrel, up about 10 cents.
Strong demand for the prompt cargoes has widened the April/May time spread to $1.30/$1.50 per barrel from under $1.00 early week, they said.
The wide front month spread was a clear reflection of the high premiums paid by traders for prompt cargoes.
On Thursday, a 150,000-barrel cargo loading April 18-22 traded at $27.50 per barrel free-on-board Singapore, about 70 cents above the value for balance April swaps.
The trader who bought the cargo was also responsible for buying up more than seven million barrels of gas oil in March.
The same trader also bought another 150,000-barrel lot at $26.80 for April 29-May loading, again reflecting the steeply backwardated market.
The backwardation has sent middle distillate stocks to one of their lowest levels in years at 4.953 million barrels for the week ending April 2, the Trade Development Board.
Overnight May Brent crude lost 33 cents to close at $18.27 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange, on top of the 60 cents it lost on Wednesday.
Gas oil on the IPE also closed weaker at $162.00 per tonne, down 3.50 from Wednesday.
The April jet fuel/gas oil regrade was quoted unchanged at -90/-70 cents, brokers said.
Fuel oil swaps edged down in thin trading following the weaker crude with April last quoted at $97.75/$99.00, down about 50 cents from Thursday.
